correctness.rationale: Each harmonic of the analytic positive-curvature support function is mapped by reflection averaging to a one-dimensional Euclidean projector; from an axis-aligned initial coefficient its exact conditional squared-energy multiplier is the average of unity and the squared cosine of the harmonic angle at all times. Parseval and the support-area identity give the exact positive infinite series. Rational angles have precisely divisible unit multipliers and a finite spectral gap elsewhere; irrational angles have no unit multipliers but arbitrarily close to one. Bounded-type Diophantine lower bounds on |sin(mα)| yield a saddle-point stretched-exponential upper bound; continued-fraction convergents of comparable size yield its matching lower bound. Strict positive curvature and Fourier convergence are proved. Standalone enumeration and area quadrature corroborate computations; no experiments replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Random symmetrization with finitely many axes is a natural boundary case of classical geometric rounding. An exact expected isoperimetric deficit and rational/irrational angular dichotomy quantify the rate obstruction, and the bounded-type irrational one-third exponent is a nongeometric convergence law for an explicitly analytic positively curved body. The effect contrasts with established continuous-axis exponential rates and is controlled by geometric Fourier energy plus arithmetic resonances, not by an arbitrary numerical slice.
